newsitem.title: CANADA: Morrison jumps after record 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Morrison jumps after record 1996 results.

text.p: Shares of takeover target Morrison Petroleums Ltd jumped to a new year high on Thursday after the company delivered sharply improved results and disclosed interest from potential competing bidders.
Morrison, the target of a C$652 million hostile offer from Canadian 88 Energy Corp, climbed 0.30 to 10.60 with 1.16 million shares changing hands in early trade in Toronto.
The company after Wednesday's market close reported record earnings and cash flow, a big jump in reserves and an improvement in finding and development costs.

Morrison chairman Gordon Stollery also told Reuters that there had been "serious interest" from potential white knights with expertise in the style of exploration in which the company was concentrating.

"Overall they were very good results," said Rob Robinson, analyst with brokerage ScotiaMcLeod in Toronto. "More particularly, their finding and development costs were superb and this just gives credence to the fact that they have an excellent exploration team."

Morrison reported that its finding and development costs -- the amount of money it takes to explore and drill for new oil and gas reserves and bring them to production -- came in at C$3.88 a barrel of oil equivalent for proven reserves and C$2.13 per BOE for proven plus probable reserves.
Canadian 88 had criticized Morrison for its high historical costs. But Stollery said on Wednesday that recent costs were high because of an accelerated land purchase program and seismic work.
"The company is well positioned. That's one of the reasons it's looked at as a takeover candidate," Robinson said.
He said the full-year results suggested a net asset value of between C$8.50 and C$9 a share, which was an increase from estimates made before Wednesday by several analysts of under C$8 a share.

There have been value estimates approaching C$11 a share, he said. But that would place a value on potential reserves that could be booked as a result of future drilling in the company's southern Alberta foothills natural gas acreage.

"That's potential. You don't pay for that," he said. "That's what a company is buying to try to extract because they're certainly not into it for a 15 percent pre-tax return." Canadian 88 has bid C$10 cash, to a maximum of C$140 million, or 1.5 of its shares for each Morrison share.
